aline_intro.speaker: aline
aline_intro.text: Your father must be the busiest man in Rwanda!

aline_intro.speaker: aline
aline_intro.text: Gasana is bringing in his beans today, and his back is not what it was. He asked if you could carry the sacks up to his storehouse.

choices.text: Only if your mother saves me some of her cooking.

aline_intro.speaker: aline
aline_intro.text: Good. Meet me on the hill when you're done. I'll be under the big tree.

aline_intro.speaker: aline
aline_intro.text: Help first, eat later! Meet me on the hill when you're done. I'll be under the big tree.

aline_intro.speaker: aline
aline_intro.text: Oh, and stop by Mama Beata's shop. She was asking for you.

aline_waiting.speaker: aline
aline_waiting.text: Gasana's beans won't carry themselves! I'll be waiting on the hill.

aline_hill.speaker: narrator
aline_hill.text: From the hilltop the whole village spreads out below: the market, the school, the football field, the red paths winding between the banana groves.

aline_hill.speaker: aline
aline_hill.text: You came! Gasana will be telling the whole market that you carried his beans.

aline_hill.speaker: aline
aline_hill.text: He'll say you were slower than his sons. And then he'll give you beans anyway.

choices.text: Offer Aline the water from Mama Beata.

aline_hill.speaker: aline
aline_hill.text: You carried that all the way up here and didn't drink it yourself? Thank you.

aline_hill.speaker: narrator
aline_hill.text: They sit together for a while. Somewhere below, a mother calls her children home for lunch.

aline_hill.speaker: aline
aline_hill.text: Do you think we'll still be here ten years from now?

aline_hill.speaker: emmanuel
aline_hill.text: Of course. This is our home.

aline_hill.speaker: aline
aline_hill.text: Then promise me you'll become a teacher. Someone who makes people think for themselves.

aline_hill.speaker: emmanuel
aline_hill.text: And you will become a doctor who makes them healthy enough to listen.

aline_hill.speaker: aline
aline_hill.text: Good. I'm holding you to it.

aline_hill.speaker: aline
aline_hill.text: Then it's a promise. Both of us.

aline_hill.speaker: aline
aline_hill.text: My little brother says he wants to be a pilot now. Last week it was a footballer.

aline_hill.speaker: emmanuel
aline_hill.text: Tell him to finish his reading first. Then he can fly wherever he wants.

aline_hill.speaker: aline
aline_hill.text: You see? You already sound like a teacher.

aline_hill.speaker: narrator
aline_hill.text: The afternoon passes slowly, the way good afternoons do.

gasana_request.speaker: gasana
gasana_request.text: Ah, Emmanuel. Aline said she would send you. Good morning.

gasana_request.speaker: emmanuel
gasana_request.text: Good morning, Gasana. She said you need some hands for the harvest.

gasana_request.speaker: gasana
gasana_request.text: Three sacks are waiting at the edge of the field. They need to be in the storehouse before the afternoon rain.

choices.text: Is your back very bad? Has anyone looked at it?

gasana_request.speaker: gasana
gasana_request.text: You sound like Aline. That girl will make a fine doctor one day. She already scolds like one.

gasana_request.speaker: gasana
gasana_request.text: Carry them on your head, the way your father taught you. The storehouse is just past the field.

gasana_waiting.speaker: gasana
gasana_waiting.text: The sacks are by the edge of the field, and the storehouse is the round hut just up the path. Take your time.

gasana_thanks.speaker: gasana
gasana_thanks.text: All three! You worked faster than my sons ever did.

gasana_thanks.speaker: gasana
gasana_thanks.text: It is never nothing when a neighbour helps. Here, take some beans home for your father.

gasana_thanks.speaker: gasana
gasana_thanks.text: Now go. I saw Aline climbing the hill. Young people should enjoy days like this.

gasana_after.speaker: gasana
gasana_after.text: Thank you again, Emmanuel. Greet your father for me.

beata_market.speaker: beata
beata_market.text: Emmanuel! There you are. Tell your father his paraffin for the lamp will come on Thursday's truck.

beata_market.speaker: beata
beata_market.text: And take this water. It is hot today, and I know you will be running up that hill before long.

choices.text: Thank you. How much do I owe you?
You know everything that happens in this village.

beata_market.speaker: beata
beata_market.text: Owe me? Put it on your father's account. The account of good neighbours.

beata_market.speaker: beata
beata_market.text: A shopkeeper hears everything. The trick is knowing what is worth repeating.

beata_default.speaker: beata
beata_default.text: Greet your father for me. And don't let Aline beat you up that hill.

uwase_greet.speaker: uwase
uwase_greet.text: Emmanuel! The examination results will be posted on this board next month.

uwase_greet.speaker: emmanuel
uwase_greet.text: I'm trying not to think about it.

uwase_greet.speaker: uwase
uwase_greet.text: I have watched you help the younger ones with their reading. You explain things patiently, and you listen. That is most of teaching.

choices.text: Do you really think I could be a teacher?
Patience is easy with children. It's the adults who are hard.

uwase_greet.speaker: uwase
uwase_greet.text: I don't think it. I know it. Come and help with the evening reading class when you can.

uwase_greet.speaker: uwase
uwase_greet.text: Then you already understand the job.

uwase_default.speaker: uwase
uwase_default.text: Next month, Emmanuel. Try to sleep before then.

claudine_greet.speaker: claudine
claudine_greet.text: Good morning, Emmanuel. My little one keeps asking when you will read him another story.

choices.text: Tell him Saturday, after the market.

claudine_greet.speaker: claudine
claudine_greet.text: He will hold you to that. He remembers everything.

claudine_greet.speaker: claudine
claudine_greet.text: The one about the hare who outwits the hyena. Every time. He knows it by heart, but he wants to hear you tell it.

claudine_default.speaker: claudine
claudine_default.text: The queue at the water point was short today. A good sign.

patrick_greet.speaker: patrick
patrick_greet.text: Emmanuel! You still owe me a rematch.

patrick_greet.speaker: emmanuel
patrick_greet.text: You only won last time because the ball went flat.

patrick_greet.speaker: patrick
patrick_greet.text: Excuses! The boys from the trading centre are coming later. Play with us.

patrick_greet.speaker: patrick
patrick_greet.text: Always Aline. Fine, fine. Next time, then.

patrick_greet.speaker: patrick
patrick_greet.text: Always helping someone. One day you will have to look after yourself, my friend.

patrick_greet.speaker: patrick
patrick_greet.text: Go on. I'll keep the ball warm.

patrick_default.speaker: patrick
patrick_default.text: The ball is still half flat. Bring a pump next time.

joseph_morning.speaker: joseph
joseph_morning.text: Back already? I thought Aline would keep you all day.

joseph_morning.speaker: emmanuel
joseph_morning.text: Gasana needs help with his beans.

joseph_morning.speaker: joseph
joseph_morning.text: Then go. A neighbour's harvest is everyone's harvest.

joseph_proud.speaker: joseph
joseph_proud.text: Gasana passed by. He says you carried his whole harvest on your head.

joseph_proud.speaker: joseph
joseph_proud.text: Three sacks is a whole harvest when your back is old. I am proud of you.

evening_radio.speaker: radio
evening_radio.text: [Static.] …the political situation in the capital remains tense… [A presenter's voice grows harsh and angry, speaking of 'enemies' living among ordinary people.]

evening_radio.speaker: narrator
evening_radio.text: Joseph reaches over and switches the radio off. The room is suddenly very quiet.

evening_radio.speaker: joseph
evening_radio.text: Some words can become weapons, my son. Never let someone convince you that another human being is your enemy simply because of who they are.

choices.text: "Why do they talk like that on the radio?"
[Say nothing. Look at the silent radio.]

evening_radio.speaker: joseph
evening_radio.text: Good. Remember it when it is hard to remember. That is when it matters.

evening_radio.speaker: joseph
evening_radio.text: Because frightened people are easier to lead. Fear can turn neighbours into a crowd. Do not let it turn you.

evening_radio.speaker: joseph
evening_radio.text: Silence is all right tonight. But one day you may have to speak. I hope you will.

evening_radio.speaker: joseph
evening_radio.text: Gasana says you worked hard today. Thank you for that.

evening_radio.speaker: joseph
evening_radio.text: Go and sleep. Tomorrow there is work, and the day after there is more.
